sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: Pigmentary retinopathy refers to a group of hereditary and acquired disorders characterized by the migration of retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) into the neurosensory retina. The most common form is Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP), a diffuse rod-cone dystrophy. While primarily an ocular disease, it frequently serves as a sentinel sign for systemic ciliopathies and metabolic disorders.

content.explanation: B: Bone-Spicule Pigmentation (perivascular); W: Waxy Disc Pallor (secondary to gliosis); A: Arteriolar Attenuation (vascular remodeling).

sections.title: Pathophysiology Workflow
content: Step 1: Genetic mutation (e.g., RHO, USH2A, RPGR) leads to rod photoreceptor dysfunction.
Step 2: Progressive shortening of rod outer segments and eventual apoptosis.
Step 3: Loss of rods leads to secondary oxidative stress and loss of trophic factors (like RdCVF), causing cone death.
Step 4: RPE cells migrate into the retina, clustering around vessels in a 'bone-spicule' pattern.
Step 5: Optic nerve gliosis occurs, resulting in the characteristic waxy pallor appearance.

sections.title: Clinical Features & Symptoms
content: Nyctalopia (Night Blindness): Often the first symptom in childhood.
Peripheral Field Loss: Starting as a mid-peripheral ring scotoma, progressing to tunnel vision.
Photopsia: Tiny shimmering lights in the peripheral field.
Central Vision Loss: Occurs late due to CME, ERM, or foveal atrophy.
Dyschromatopsia: Late-stage loss of color discrimination.

branches: Metabolic: Vitamin A deficiency, Refsum Disease

sections.title: Critical Red Flags
content: Sudden vision drop: Suggestive of Cystoid Macular Edema (CME).
Unilateral presentation: Highly suspicious for Pseudo-RP (RP is bilateral).
History of high-dose Vitamin E: Can accelerate disease progression in some forms.
Presence of hearing loss: Must rule out Usher Syndrome immediately.

sections.title: Management & Treatment
content: Vitamin A Palmitate: 15,000 IU/day (controversial, monitor liver enzymes).
Omega-3 Fatty Acids: 1200mg/day may slow ERG decline.
CME Treatment: Topical or oral Carbonic Anhydrase Inhibitors (Acetazolamide/Dorzolamide).
UV Protection: Dark amber wrap-around sunglasses to reduce phototoxicity.
Low Vision Aids: Bioptics, magnifiers, and mobility training.

sections.title: Gene Therapy: Luxturna (Voretigene Neparvovec)
content: 1. Confirm Biallelic RPE65 mutation via genetic testing.
2. Pars Plana Vitrectomy (PPV) performed by vitreoretinal surgeon.
3. Subretinal injection of AAV2 vector carrying RPE65 cDNA.
4. Restoration of the visual cycle and rod function.

sections.title: Landmark Clinical Pearls
content: The 'Mizuo-Nakamura' phenomenon: Characteristic of Oguri disease, not classic RP.
Preserved peripapillary RPE: Often a sign of CRB1 mutations.
Bone spicules follow the vessels: Because the vessels provide the scaffold for RPE migration.
XL-RP: Check female carriers for a 'tapetal-like' retinal sheen.

sections.title: Surgical Complications
content: Posterior Subcapsular Cataract (PSC): Extremely common; manage with surgery.
Zonular Weakness: Higher risk of lens subluxation during phacoemulsification.
Vitreous Syneresis: Increased risk of retinal tears and detachment.
Epiretinal Membrane: Can cause significant tractional macular distortion.

sections.title: Recent Advances & Landmark Studies
sections.content: The Berson Study (1993) established the role of Vitamin A Palmitate. Recent focus has shifted to Optogenetics (using viral vectors to make surviving cells light-sensitive) and Stem Cell therapy to replace the RPE layer. The ARGUS II Retinal Prosthesis, while now discontinued commercially, proved the feasibility of electronic retinal bypass in end-stage disease.

sections.title: Pediatric Considerations
content: Leber Congenital Amaurosis (LCA): The severe, infantile-onset form of pigmentary retinopathy.
Oculodigital Reflex: Frequent eye poking (Franceschetti's sign) to induce phosphenes.
Nystagmus: Develops early in severe pediatric cases due to poor fixation.
Genetic Counseling: Essential for families to understand recurrence risk.
